subject: BrightCart: urgent -- cache behavior causing p99 spikes and 503s
messages:
From: Michael Turner <m.turner@brightcart.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-28 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: sudden p99 and 503s this morning

Hannah —

We started seeing p99 latency jump and ~2% 503 rate around 09:30 EDT after a marketing surge. Attach a couple of sample traces and the error snippet. Our team observed a recurring pattern where certain user queries always hit the same GPU and then subsequent requests to that shard queue up. This is impacting the checkout flow (payments) and exec is asking for a timeline. We're on a tight renewal decision with Procurement next week. Appreciate urgent help.

—Michael Turner

Michael —

Thanks for the fast heads-up and the logs. We're looking now. Quick notes from an initial triage:
- Control plane shows a spike in requests pinned to a small set of model workers between 09:25–09:50 EDT.
- Observed persistent KV cache misses for a set of prefixes used heavily by your search autocomplete route.
- One worker reported HOL blocking metrics (queue depth growing while other workers idle).

I'm escalating to ops and runtime leads (cc Marissa and Jonas). Can you confirm if BrightCart changed any routing rules or started a new campaign at 09:00? Also keep any new customer traffic samples coming. We'll follow up with a mitigation plan in the next 45 min.

—Hannah
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-kv-config-diff.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Michael Turner <m.turner@brightcart.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-28 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: sudden p99 and 503s this morning

Adding our runtime diagnostics:
- Evidence points to two related issues compounding: (1) the KV prefix-store isn't honoring TTL/eviction hints for the new prefix set; (2) batching lanes for the affected model class are being starved by long-running decoding requests that were routed without prefix cache hits.
- The config diff (attached) shows a recent change that widened the hot-prefix mapping to include a dynamic prefix bucket; that caused more entries to be retained on a subset of workers. With the traffic skew, those workers hit memory pressure and eviction churn — thrash.

Immediate mitigations we can attempt now (non-disruptive -> more invasive):
1) Short-term: apply per-prefix eviction override to force aggressive pruning of large prefixes (safe, non-disruptive, immediate)
2) Near-term: re-route a % of requests to warm pool (model variant with trimmed KV) to reduce hot-worker load (requires config push + 2-min warm-up)
3) Fallback: scale up dedicated lanes for BrightCart (reserved burst) — requires approval.

I'll apply step (1) now unless BrightCart requests otherwise. We'll monitor for the next 30 min and report back.

—Marissa
VP, Runtime Operations
attachments: redwood-kv-config-diff.txt

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-06-28 12:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: sudden p99 and 503s this morning

Applied eviction override and tightened prefix retention for BrightCart's prefix set. Observed:
- p99 fell from ~1.9s to ~820ms within two minutes
- 503 rate dropped from 2.1% to 0.3% over 10 minutes
- Worker queue depth normalized but still shows occasional spikes correlated with long generation requests (possible HOL blocking).

Next steps (action items):
- Hannah to coordinate a canary of routing 10% traffic to the trimmed model variant (H: start 13:15 EDT).
- Markus to review batching lane priorities and add temporary lane preemption for BrightCart (M: aim 14:00 EDT).
- Marissa to prepare a short exec slide (cause, mitigation, residual risk).

We'll keep you in the loop.

—Jonas
Head of SRE

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Turner <m.turner@brightcart.com>, BrightCart SRE <ops@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Post-mortem draft + exec notes for 16:00 briefing

Team —

Brief update for the executive briefing at 16:00: we traced the incident to an unintended config change to the hot-prefix mapping which expanded the prefix bucket and prevented timely eviction on a subset of workers. The traffic spike from BrightCart's marketing campaign amplified the effect and caused eviction churn (cache thrash) and head-of-line blocking in a few batching lanes. The immediate override and a 10% routing canary to a trimmed model variant reduced p99 and 503s.

Impact summary:
- Customer: BrightCart (Checkout + Search autocomplete)
- Duration: ~09:25–12:30 EDT (impact window, resolved to acceptable thresholds by 12:30)
- Severity: P1 -> customer-facing degradation; exec notified
- Root cause: hot-prefix mapping change + traffic skew -> eviction thrash and KV miss amplification

Proposed follow-ups (next 72 hrs):
- Roll back the config expansion and implement a staged rollout safeguard for prefix-mapping changes. (Owner: Runtime Config)
- Add a dynamic hot-prefix admission controller that limits retained entries per-worker by memory signal. (Owner: Runtime)
- Short-term lane preemption policy for customers in renewal/expansion windows. (Owner: Product Ops)
- Customer remediation: 1 month credit + joint load-walk and runbook update. (Sales/CS)

Attachments: exec-slide-draft (attached), config-diff (attached).

Michael — can you confirm if the 16:00 exec slot still holds? We'll present the short deck and the immediate mitigations.

Thanks — Hannah
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
